Tuesday, November 10, 2026

Space & Defense Daily — Tuesday, Nov 10, 2026

Europe, Ukraine, the U.S. and NATO agreed in Abu Dhabi to review Europe's post-war security architecture as trilateral talks with Russia opened; France ordered two IRIS military imaging satellites from Airbus and Thales Alenia Space for more than €1.5 billion; Congress returned for a lame-duck session with the $1.5 trillion defense request effectively dead and the NDAA still unfinished.

← NewerWed, Nov 11, 2026All briefingsOlder →Mon, Nov 9, 2026
NATOEuropean UnionUnited StatesEuropean spaceGlobal space & defense

Top stories: European partners, Ukraine, the U.S. and NATO agreed in Abu Dhabi to review Europe's post-war security architecture as the first trilateral talks with Russia since February began. France ordered two IRIS military Earth-observation satellites from Airbus and Thales Alenia Space for more than €1.5 billion. Congress is back for a six-week lame-duck session, with the Pentagon's $1.5 trillion budget effectively dead and the NDAA still unfinished.

NATO

  • Ahead of the trilateral talks with Russia, the EU, France, Germany, Italy, the UK, Ukraine, the U.S. and NATO issued a joint statement backing robust security guarantees for Ukraine and a "strong post-war European security architecture," and said a strong NATO will remain central to collective defence. (Council of the EU)
  • Politico reports that this is the first U.S.–Ukraine–Russia meeting in nine months, and that Witkoff and Kushner are pushing to widen the talks to cover Europe's future security and to give Europe a seat at the table. (Politico Europe)
  • Former NATO Secretary General Anders Fogh Rasmussen said Europe must stop "begging" for a seat at the peace talks and should instead make itself indispensable by bringing assets to the table. (Euronews)
  • In eastern Latvia, about 3,000 troops and 1,000 vehicles from the Canadian-led multinational brigade are rehearsing long-distance moves and sustainment in Resolute Reforger 2026. (FLANK)
  • On Nov. 11, Rutte will join the Atlantic Future Forum aboard the UK carrier HMS Prince of Wales in Oslo, where he will tour the ship with UK Defence Secretary Wes Streeting. (NATO)

European Union

  • At a Nov. 9 Eurogroup meeting with NATO's Rutte, EU finance ministers were told to reorder national budget priorities so they can fund higher defence spending before fiscal-rule flexibility ends in 2028. Commissioner Dombrovskis pointed to more than €20 billion available in the second SAFE loan round. (EU Perspectives)
  • Council figures put EU national defence spending at about €418 billion in 2025 and an estimated €454 billion in 2026 (2.4% of GDP), and Eurogroup chief Pierrakakis called for joint procurement and private capital for defence start-ups. (2EU Brussels)
  • The Commission launched a "European defence: protect what matters" campaign in ten northern and eastern flank states. It says SAFE has disbursed almost €13.5 billion across 11 member states, with a second round of up to €21.3 billion now open. (European Commission DG DEFIS)

United States

  • Congress returned Nov. 9 for a lame-duck session after big Democratic midterm gains. Analysts say the $1.5 trillion defense request is effectively dead, a $350 billion reconciliation bill is a long shot, another stopgap funding bill is likely before the Dec. 11 deadline, and the NDAA is still caught in disputes over Iran and other partisan provisions. (Air & Space Forces Magazine)
  • Anduril unveiled three satellite payloads it has already tested in orbit, including an infrared sensor built to track spacecraft in Earth's shadow. (SpaceNews)
  • The Space Force activated U.S. Space Forces Special Operations Command (SPACEFOR-SOC) at MacDill AFB on Nov. 2 to embed small space, cyber and intelligence teams with special operations forces. (Military.com)
  • At Global MILSATCOM in London, Space Force leaders pressed European allies to co-invest in resilient, interoperable satellite communications and said allies are "sovereign teammates," not passive partners. (U.S. Space Force)
  • Lockheed Martin received more than $1 billion in contract modifications: $826 million for JASSM/LRASM, which lifts that contract to $10.48 billion, and $257 million for MK 48 torpedoes. (The Defense News)
  • L3Harris said it received $157 million in U.S. Army orders for vehicle radios and Hawkeye 4 Lite satellite terminals. (Defence Industry Europe)
  • SpaceX's classified USSF-627 Falcon 9 launch from Vandenberg slipped from Monday. It now targets tonight, Nov. 10, with a window opening at 6:49 p.m. PT and a backup on Nov. 11. (SpaceX)
  • NASA opened applications for a new astronaut class through Dec. 3 to staff Artemis and the lunar base. Artemis III will practice docking with the SpaceX and Blue Origin landers in Earth orbit next summer. (Los Angeles Times / AP)
  • NASA's twin ESCAPADE smallsats, built by Rocket Lab, completed the agency's first powered Earth flybys toward Mars and are due to arrive in September 2027. (SpaceNews)
  • Rocket Lab is raising Electron and Neutron launch prices, citing high demand in a constrained launch market. (SpaceNews)

European space

  • France's DGA ordered two IRIS optical spy satellites from Airbus (prime) and Thales Alenia Space for more than €1.5 billion to replace the CSO constellation. The first is due to be operational in 2033, and the program is open to partner nations. (Defense News)
  • ESA's OHB-built Hera returned its first close-up image of the Didymos binary asteroid as it begins studying the aftermath of the DART impact. (SpaceWatch.Global)
  • Frontex chief Hans Leijtens and ESA Director General Josef Aschbacher signed a joint letter in Warsaw to deepen cooperation on satellite Earth observation for border surveillance. (The Continental)

Global space & defense

  • Russia struck 10 Ukrainian regions overnight, hitting five major substations, causing outages in Kyiv, Kharkiv and Dnipropetrovsk and killing two people, as the Abu Dhabi talks opened. Lavrov said Moscow won't agree to an immediate ceasefire. (Reuters via StreetInsider)
  • China's Long March 12 launch of nine Guowang broadband satellites on Nov. 9 brings the state constellation to about 240 satellites in orbit. (London Daily News)
  • AST SpaceMobile plans up to 50 satellites for a joint venture with Rakuten, which is in line for up to ¥148 billion ($1 billion) in Japanese subsidies for a sovereign direct-to-device network by March 2029. (SpaceNews)
